title: A small shared step for NPC1 and Tay-Sachs families

sentences.text: At Hide & Seek Foundation, we support NPC1 families; CATS supports families affected by Tay-Sachs disease.
Both diseases involve material building up in cells’ recycling compartments, called lysosomes, although the stored materials differ.
The atlas also proposes a shared protein-folding problem, but this connection is inferred, contested and below 0.5 confidence (0.45), not a proven basis for shared treatment.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: The International Niemann-Pick Disease Registry (INPDR) and SOAR research network already include NPC1; we could explore lessons from their approaches.

The National Multicentre Study of the Natural History of Acid Sphingo-myelinase Deficiency in Adults and Children studies SMPD1 disease; adapting its design for NPC1 is a possibility to investigate, not confirmed access.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please confirm whether unesterified cholesterol accumulation in cultured skin cells and elevated circulating C-triol also occur in SMPD1 disease, and check low cholesterol esterification across the proposed comparisons.
The resource comparison flags 13 further unlisted NPC1 features for the SMPD1 study and 16 for the Pompe grant; missing records should not be treated as proof of absence.
We should review differences in enzyme deficiency, sphingolipid breakdown in SMPD1, and glycogen breakdown plus one unspecified mechanism in Pompe.
Before considering the AMDA Research Grant, confirm whether it accepts related conditions beyond Pompe.
We should also check which individual gene variants might respond to protein-stabilising approaches, rather than assume shared eligibility.

Could we jointly send one enquiry to the International Niemann-Pick Disease Alliance asking whether the SMPD1 natural history study could include NPC1, with the laboratory-feature checks above attached?
Which variants in GBA1, HEXA, NPC1 and GAA are “amenable”—potentially responsive—to a chaperone, as GLA variants are classified for migalastat?
Let us keep any treatment discussion limited to published evidence to discuss with a neurologist.
Dear Cure and Action for Tay-Sachs (CATS) Foundation,
I’m writing on behalf of Hide & Seek Foundation to invite a modest collaboration.
Our communities share a lysosomal-storage connection.
Could we send the proposed enquiry together this month?
We would welcome your perspective on the questions families want answered first.
[Your name], on behalf of Hide & Seek Foundation
